audit.whatIsWrong: Our chart (Skill, Skill, Skill, Ziggs, Skill, Ziggs, Ziggs) disagrees with the already-audited mirror on five of seven rows.
audit.why: The mirror (sett__ziggs) records Ziggs / Skill / Sett / Sett / Sett / Sett / Skill and notes that it fixed a chart that was 'the inverse of its own whys in both layers'. mirror-fix.js overwrites disagreements, so I aligned to the mirror and rewrote the four whys that would otherwise argue the opposite side.
audit.corrected: Ziggs / Skill / Sett / Sett / Sett / Sett / Skill — paired full/content rows with ratings, plus matching whys.

audit.why: Level 6 as Sett's window is right and already on the page: The Show Stopper is 120/100/80s but only 400 range, so it needs Flash or Facebreaker to reach you, and spikes[1] says exactly that. Your counter-spike is Mega Inferno Bomb at 5000 range on 120/95/70.
sources: kits: sett R range 400 cd 120/100/80; ziggs R range 5000 cd 120/95/70

audit.whatIsWrong: Two real gaps. Facebreaker is described as a pull-stun with no conditions, when Riot's text says it only stuns enemies on OPPOSITE sides of him — alone on one side you are slowed, not stunned. And nothing on the page says Haymaker's centre is true damage.
audit.why: Riot: 'Sett pulls in all enemies on opposite sides of him, dealing damage and stunning them. If enemies were only on one side, they are slowed instead of stunned.' Range 490, cooldown 16/14.5/13/11.5/10. Haymaker stores damage taken as Grit and spends it for a shield plus true damage in the centre — so your own poke fuels his shield, and buying resistances is the wrong answer.
audit.corrected: Facebreaker is 490 range and 16s at rank 1, and it only stuns if there is something on the far side of him — stand clear of his minions and you take a slow instead. Haymaker's centre is true damage, so resistances do not save you, and the poke you land is the Grit that powers it.
sources: kits: sett E text/range 490/cd 16-10, W Grit + true damage centre

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.cooldowns named Facebreaker as matchup-defining but gave no number.
audit.why: Facebreaker 16s at rank 1 and Haymaker 18s at rank 1 are the two timers that decide whether a step-up is free.

edits.before: Level 3 your spacing past his E stun and W keeps the lane in your favour.
edits.after: Level 3 Facebreaker's 490 pull plus true-damage Haymaker flips any trade.

edits.before: Through 4-5 your range and poke out-value his short-range kit.
edits.after: Through 4-5 the Grit he banks off your poke becomes his shield.

edits.before: With items your Liandry's poke and shove pin him under tower again.
edits.after: With items his Grit shield and raw health blunt your first-item burst.

edits.before: Late your waveclear and R siege out-scale his single-target engage.
edits.after: Late your siege out-ranges him, but one Show Stopper reaches your line.

edits.before: Out-poke Sett with Q while he has no gap-closer — punish his Haymaker (W) grit build-up and E stun range by staying spaced behind minions.
edits.after: Haymaker's centre is true damage — resistances do not save you, and your own poke feeds the Grit that powers it. Stay outside Facebreaker's 490.

edits.before: The pull-stun starts his combo — stay off the line between him and units. Commit on its cooldown, never into it.
edits.after: Facebreaker reaches 490 and only stuns with enemies on both sides — alone on one side you are merely slowed.

edits.before: - Sett Facebreaker: matchup-defining — The pull-stun starts his combo — stay off the line between him and units. Count it out loud if you must. - Your W Satchel has one job: the moment it all goes wrong. - The R has one too: the moment it all goes right.
edits.after: - Sett Facebreaker: 16 seconds at rank 1 and only 490 range, and Haymaker is 18 — with both down he cannot hold you still. - Your W Satchel has one job: the moment it all goes wrong. - The R has one too: the moment it all goes right.

notes: Chart aligned to the already-audited mirror (Ziggs / Skill / Sett / Sett / Sett / Sett / Skill) as one atomic group, with the four contradicting whys rewritten to match. I am not confident the mirror's chart is right — it hands Sett four straight stages in a matchup Ziggs wins 64% — but the mirror is authoritative here and mirror-fix.js would overwrite any disagreement I introduced, so I matched it and raised it in questionsForUser rather than fight it. Both packet suspectNames ('Show Stopper', 'Sett's Show Stopper') are inflections of The Show Stopper, not fabrications — left alone. Best new fact: Facebreaker only stuns with enemies on opposite sides of Sett; one-sided, it is a slow. Second: Haymaker's centre is true damage and is fuelled by the Grit your own poke gives him. whys[5] and spikes[2] still name Liandry's while the report itemization says Blackfire Torch — champion-level inconsistency, not touched.
